title: RESTful API Design Conventions & Standards
keyTechniques: Use plural nouns for resource endpoints (e.g., /api/users, /api/tasks) rather than verbs (/api/getUsers)
Map HTTP verbs cleanly to CRUD actions: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (remove)
Return standard HTTP status codes: 200 (OK), 201 (Created), 400 (Bad Request), 401 (Unauthorized), 404 (Not Found), 500 (Internal Error)
Use consistent JSON response envelope structures across all endpoints (e.g. { status: 'success'|'error', data, message })
avoid: Do not use GET requests to perform data mutation actions
Do not return status 200 OK when an internal server error or validation failure occurs
Do not mix inconsistent casing in JSON keys (prefer camelCase for keys across all endpoints)
